clue.text: Strikes for money

definitions.meaning: to pound is to hit hard, so strikes in the verb sense
the pound is British currency, and in the plural means sums of money

explanation.surface: Workers walk out on strike to get more pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pounds are both blows struck repeatedly and units of British currency, so the two senses share one spelling.

clue.text: Tread warily on weeds in fields

parts.note: to pad is to walk softly and quietly
docks are coarse broad-leaved weeds

explanation.surface: Walking carefully through weeds in the meadows.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddocks are small enclosed fields, usually for horses.

clue.text: Without regularity, oddly?

definitions.meaning: irregularly, not in a smooth or consistent way
read as ..., in a manner that is not even, as an odd number is

explanation.surface: Something done irregularly and strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things irregularly is the plain sense, and not-even numbers are odd ones, giving the second.

clue.text: Democrat joining revolutionary movement — that's odd

parts.note: a roll is a turning-over motion, a movement that revolves

explanation.surface: A Democrat joining a revolution seems strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comically strange or quirky can be called odd in a humorous way.

clue.text: Finish off Animal Farm, the novel for holiday

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so these letters are put into a new order
the finish of a word is its closing letter, so take only the end of Animal

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student wants to finish reading Orwell's Animal Farm over the school break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun describing Orwell's book; it is the anagram signal, rearranging L, FARM and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-term is a short school holiday in the middle of a British school term.

clue.text: Released after confession without any charge

indicators.note: the released word comes after the confession word in the answer

parts.note: an admission is a confession of guilt
set free means released

explanation.surface: A suspect let go after confessing, with no charges brought.
explanation.definitionFit: Free entry means no price is charged to get in, the sense the phrase has on a sign.

clue.text: Warns in advance about bloke imprisoned by enemy

indicators.note: imprisoned by puts the about-and-bloke pieces inside the enemy word

parts.note: foes are the enemy
re means about or concerning
a bod is a British slang word for a person or bloke

explanation.surface: A warning is given about a man held captive by enemies.
explanation.definitionFit: To forebode is to predict or presage something bad, giving an early warning.

clue.text: Caused by wind making one ail dreadfully

indicators.note: dreadfully implies the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wind making a person feel very unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeolian or eolian deposits are those carried and laid down by wind, named after Aeolus the wind god.

clue.text: Upset some wine and spirit? Hell!

indicators.note: upset in a down clue tips the wine-and-spirit run over so it reads backwards

parts.note: red is a type of wine
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Spilling wine and spirits brings a cry of annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: One reversal turns both pieces, so REDRUM read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described as hell is very unpleasant, and 'it was murder' is the British idiom for that.

clue.text: As result of couple's act, love follows

indicators.note: the love letter comes after the duet in the answer

parts.note: a duet is a performance by a pair
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A double act wins applause, and romance comes after.
explanation.definitionFit: Owing to or because of a cause is the meaning of the phrase, a prepositional synonym.

clue.text: Poet includes appeal backing fighter for independence

indicators.note: the poet's name holds the next piece within it

parts.note: Homer is the Greek epic poet of the Iliad

indicators.note: backing means the word for appeal is read in reverse

parts.note: a lure is an attraction or appeal

explanation.surface: A poet takes up a cause in support of a freedom fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of Home Rule campaigned for Irish self-government, so was a fighter for independence.

clue.text: Having a problem, in a sense? Doctor had for trial

definitions.text: Having a problem, in a sense?

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a hearing is a trial in court

explanation.surface: A physician's patient is being tried for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person; it is the anagram signal, making HARDOF from HAD FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deaf or partly deaf has a problem with one of the five senses.

clue.text: Part of test and its possible location for top men

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls, a part of a cricket test match
Lord's is the London cricket ground where test matches are played

explanation.surface: A section of an exam and where it might be held are linked to the bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'test' looks like an exam but means a cricket test match; LORD'S is a famous London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlords are rulers with supreme power over others, the people at the top.

clue.text: British people giving support

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: The British public rally round to help.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a prop or strut, a thing that holds something up.

clue.text: Achieve economic goals — 8 or 20, 12 or 15, using 23 or 14 1 across

parts.note: the entries at 8 and 20 are murder and waste, both senses of the verb to end a life or squander
a brace is a pair of game birds; cock and crow are two bird names
using means by means of, the preposition with
a solitaire is a single gem, one jewel; fourteen pounds make a single unit of weight in the imperial system

explanation.surface: Instructions for being efficient, written as a chain of references to other entries.
explanation.walkthrough: Each cross-reference stands for one word of the proverb: 8 MURDER or 20 WASTE, 12 BRACE or 15 COCK+CROW, and 23 SOLITAIRE (a single gem) or 14 (from 14-down) with 1 across, 14 POUNDS, which is a stone in British weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb means achieving two aims with one action, which is economy of effort.

clue.text: Cut down damaged trees in quarter

parts.note: to trim is to cut down

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of trees are broken and reformed

explanation.surface: Felling ruined trees in a district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter' looks like a district but means a period of three months; 'damaged' makes ESTER from TREES.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is a span of three months, a quarter of a year.

clue.text: Prepare to shoot some Native Americans when sun comes up

parts.note: to cock a gun is to make it ready to fire
the Crow are a Native American people

explanation.surface: Readying a gun for some Native Americans at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The crowing of the rooster happens at dawn, so the word means daybreak.

clue.text: Throw out of aircraft, one of which is not turning up outside

parts.note: a jet is one example of an aircraft

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the little word is
in a down entry turning up reads the word upward, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dumping something from an aeroplane that refuses to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of aircraft' does double duty in the surface: the definition is 'Throw out of aircraft', and 'one of which' refers back to aircraft for JET.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to discard cargo from a ship or aircraft, throwing it overboard.

clue.text: See 13
Silly types, swallowing small mixed drinks

indicators.note: swallowing means the silly people take the small letter inside

parts.note: twits are silly people

explanation.surface: Fools gulping down small cocktails.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist is a drink made by mixing two different beverages, such as gin and brandy.

clue.text: Tragic heroine that is betrayed in the middle

indicators.note: the betrayed word sits in the middle of the abbreviation

parts.note: sold out, or sold, means betrayed

explanation.surface: A doomed heroine is betrayed at the centre of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the lover in the Tristan legend and Wagner's opera, a tragic heroine.

clue.text: Desolate area in Wild West

indicators.note: the area letter is placed inside the reworked letters
wild signals that the letters of West are disordered

explanation.surface: A barren region in the American frontier lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild West' looks like one phrase but 'Wild' is the anagram signal; WEST rearranged and opened around A gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste land is barren and empty, so as an adjective it is a synonym for bleak and uninhabited.

clue.text: Power in a current missile that could bring plane down

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics

indicators.note: the power letter goes inside the missile word

parts.note: a rocket is a missile

explanation.surface: An electrical power supply feeding a missile that could shoot down an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A region of turbulent descending air makes an aircraft drop suddenly in flight.

clue.text: Piano used in old-time musical entertainment

indicators.note: the piano letter is put to use inside the old-time pieces

parts.note: an era is a period of time
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A piano is played in an old-fashioned musical show.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is staged drama set to music, a form of musical entertainment.

clue.text: Game one plays that's strange to Israeli

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the phrase are oddly arranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pastime someone enjoys seems unfamiliar to a person from Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a card or peg game played by a single person, hence a game one plays alone.

clue.text: New money invested in neuroscience

indicators.note: the money is set inside the word that follows, like funds put into a venture

explanation.surface: Fresh funds are being put into brain research.
explanation.definitionFit: This European currency was introduced in 1999 to 2002, so it was new money replacing older coins.

clue.text: Poet's always in coach, cheapest form of travel

indicators.note: the poetic word goes inside the coach word

parts.note: a stage is a stagecoach
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A poet always rides in a coach, the cheapest way to travel.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the lowest-fare accommodation on a passenger ship, the cheapest class of travel.

clue.text: Scientist, like Newton, considered noteworthy?

parts.note: noteworthy is read literally: a scientist who, like Isaac Newton before him, was pictured on a Bank of England banknote

explanation.surface: A scientist as distinguished as Newton.
explanation.walkthrough: Newton appeared on the old British one-pound note, and the naturalist in the answer on the ten-pound note, so both were literally worthy of a note.
explanation.definitionFit: The naturalist who proposed natural selection is a scientist who appeared on the British ten-pound note.
